blocks.text: 1. Contextual Retrieval
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447444520-26166265.png
Contextual Retrieval closes out the Retrieval module by tying every earlier idea together: retrieved chunks now carry richer surrounding context.
It closes the Retrieval module by combining contextual chunking with retrieval time enrichment.
2. Bringing Contextual Chunking Into Retrieval
Contextual Chunking enriched chunk text before embedding, back in the Chunking module, by prepending document context.
Contextual retrieval extends that same idea across the full retrieval pipeline.
3. Retrieval Module Recap
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447444520-172342524.png
Fourteen topics covered searching, transforming queries, and combining strategies.
Contextual retrieval closes the module by enriching what actually gets returned.

blocks.text: 4. Combining Parent Document And Contextual Chunking

blocks.alt: Combining Parent Document And Contextual Chunking
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447444521-260935832.png
As with search small, return large, revisited in Parent Document Retrieval, returning a parent already restores surrounding context.
Contextual retrieval layers contextual chunking's enrichment on top of that same returned context.
5. Attaching Retrieval Metadata To Results
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447444521-644173955.png
As with hierarchical chunking and metadata in Hierarchical Chunking, a returned chunk can carry its ancestor path, source, and retrieval score together.
This gives the downstream model everything it needs to judge and cite the result properly.
6. Contextual Retrieval Across Ensemble Members
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447444733-151778788.png
As with independent retrieval, then fusion in Ensemble Retrieval, each ensemble member's results can carry their own enriched context before fusion.
The final merged results stay rich in context regardless of which member found them.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A chunk found through sparse retrieval and a chunk found through dense retrieval both carry the same enriched context once contextual retrieval is applied uniformly across the ensemble.

blocks.text: 7. Balancing Richness Against Context Budget
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447444733-235663264.png
As with context window considerations in Parent Document Retrieval, richer context per result means fewer results fit in the model's available budget.
That same tradeoff reappears here, now applied to every enrichment technique combined.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Stacking parent document retrieval, contextual chunking enrichment, and metadata all at once produces very rich but also very large results, meaning fewer of them can fit within a model's fixed context budget.

blocks.text: 8. Retrieval As The Completed Stage
Every technique covered across this entire module fed into producing the best possible retrieval result.
This closes the Retrieval module before Re-Ranking, the next module, begins.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When Contextual Retrieval Deserves The Added Enrichment

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Contextual Retrieval Deserves The Added Enrichment
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447444733-473321365.png
Complex documents where source and structure matter benefit most.
Simple, self contained chunk collections need only minimal contextual enrichment.
10. Worked Example
The example below demonstrates attaching ancestor path and source metadata to a retrieved result.

code.content:
retrieved_chunk = {
    "text": "Refunds require a receipt and must be requested within thirty days.",
    "ancestor_path": ["Customer Handbook", "Chapter 4: Billing", "4.2 Refunds"],
    "source": "handbook_v3.pdf",
    "retrieval_score": 0.91,
}

def build_contextual_result(chunk):
    # Attach ancestor path and source metadata to the result
    path_text = " > ".join(chunk["ancestor_path"])
    return {
        "text": chunk["text"],
        "context_summary": f"From {chunk['source']}, section: {path_text}",
        "score": chunk["retrieval_score"],
    }

result = build_contextual_result(retrieved_chunk)
print("Retrieved chunk before enrichment:")
print(f"  {retrieved_chunk['text']!r}\n")

print("Contextually enriched result:")
print(f"  text: {result['text']!r}")
print(f"  context: {result['context_summary']!r}")
print(f"  score: {result['score']}")

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Running this example shows the raw chunk text paired with a readable source and section summary, giving the downstream model far more to work with than text alone.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Stacking every enrichment technique at once without checking the resulting context budget impact.
Forgetting to attach consistent metadata across results from different ensemble members.
Applying heavy contextual enrichment to already short, self contained chunks that need none.
Never measuring whether richer context actually improves the downstream model's answers.

blocks.text: 12. Retrieval: Module Complete

items: Semantic Search introduced finding chunks by meaning rather than exact wording.
Keyword Search covered exact term matching that complements semantic search.
Hybrid Search covered combining semantic and keyword retrieval into one system.
Dense Retrieval and Sparse Retrieval revisited embeddings through a retrieval specific lens.
Metadata Retrieval covered using structured fields as an active retrieval signal.
Query Expansion, Query Rewriting, and Query Transformation covered improving the query itself.
Multi-Query, Self-Query, Multi-Hop, and Ensemble Retrieval covered advanced retrieval strategies.
Parent Document Retrieval covered restoring fuller context from a matched fragment.
Contextual Retrieval closed the module by combining enrichment techniques together.
Next up: Re-Ranking, covering how retrieved results get reordered for even better final relevance.
